sentence: ___ the ticket was expensive, I visited my family.
setupText: Choose the connector showing that the visit happened despite the expense.
taskText: ___ the ticket was expensive, I visited my family.
text: Choose the connector showing that the visit happened despite the expense. ___ the ticket was expensive, I visited my family.
explanation: Although presents the expense as an obstacle that did not stop the visit.

rationales.Because: Because would make the expense a reason for visiting.
rationales.Although: Although presents the expense as an obstacle that did not stop the visit.
rationales.Until: Until gives an endpoint in time, not a contrast with expense.
rationales.So that: So that would make the ticket's expense the purpose of the visit.

sentence: The outdoor concert stopped ___ a storm.
setupText: Choose the completion that correctly introduces the reason in this sentence.
taskText: The outdoor concert stopped ___ a storm.
text: Choose the completion that correctly introduces the reason in this sentence. The outdoor concert stopped ___ a storm.
explanation: Because of introduces the noun phrase a storm as the reason.

rationales.because: Because needs a clause, such as because a storm began.
rationales.although: Although needs a clause here and would introduce contrast, not the requested reason.
rationales.because of: Because of introduces the noun phrase a storm as the reason.
rationales.so that: So that needs a clause expressing a purpose or result, not just a storm.

sentence: I prepared the salad ___ my friend cooked the rice.
setupText: Choose the word showing that the two activities happened at the same time.
taskText: I prepared the salad ___ my friend cooked the rice.
text: Choose the word showing that the two activities happened at the same time. I prepared the salad ___ my friend cooked the rice.
explanation: While presents the two people's cooking activities as overlapping.

rationales.after: After puts salad preparation later than cooking the rice.
rationales.because: Because gives a reason rather than explicitly showing simultaneous activities.
rationales.while: While presents the two people's cooking activities as overlapping.

sentence: Please wait here ___ the receptionist returns.
setupText: Choose the word meaning the waiting continues up to the named time.
taskText: Please wait here ___ the receptionist returns.
text: Choose the word meaning the waiting continues up to the named time. Please wait here ___ the receptionist returns.
explanation: Until makes the receptionist's return the endpoint of waiting.

rationales.until: Until makes the receptionist's return the endpoint of waiting.
rationales.after: After would place the waiting later than the return.
rationales.because: Because gives a reason and does not set the end of the wait.
rationales.although: Although would contrast waiting with the return, not mark an endpoint.

sentence: I went to the bank ___ pay in a cheque.
setupText: Choose the completion expressing the purpose of going to the bank.
taskText: I went to the bank ___ pay in a cheque.
text: Choose the completion expressing the purpose of going to the bank. I went to the bank ___ pay in a cheque.
explanation: To plus pay gives the purpose of going to the bank.

rationales.because: Because would need a full clause, such as because I needed to pay in a cheque.
rationales.so that: So that needs a subject and verb, such as so that I could pay.
rationales.to: To plus pay gives the purpose of going to the bank.
rationales.for: For does not directly introduce the base verb pay in this purpose phrase.

sentence: The guide spoke slowly ___ everyone could understand the directions.
setupText: Choose the connector expressing the purpose of speaking slowly.
taskText: The guide spoke slowly ___ everyone could understand the directions.
text: Choose the connector expressing the purpose of speaking slowly. The guide spoke slowly ___ everyone could understand the directions.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-a2-506:So that with a different subject
explanation: So that introduces the intended benefit for a different subject, everyone.

rationales.even though: Even though presents understanding as a fact in contrast, not the guide's purpose.
rationales.so that: So that introduces the intended benefit for a different subject, everyone.
rationales.because of: Because of cannot directly introduce the full clause everyone could understand.
rationales.until: Until sets an endpoint rather than stating the intended benefit.

sentence: We paid ___ we checked the bill carefully.
setupText: Choose the connector placing payment later than checking the bill.
taskText: We paid ___ we checked the bill carefully.
text: Choose the connector placing payment later than checking the bill. We paid ___ we checked the bill carefully.
explanation: After places the completed check before payment.

rationales.before: Before would put payment ahead of checking.
rationales.because: Because gives checking as a reason rather than directly stating the requested order.
rationales.while: While would make payment overlap with checking.
rationales.after: After places the completed check before payment.

sentence: Check the platform number before the train ___.
setupText: Choose the usual verb form for a future event after 'before' in this instruction.
taskText: Check the platform number before the train ___.
text: Choose the usual verb form for a future event after 'before' in this instruction. Check the platform number before the train ___.
explanation: A future time clause after 'before' normally uses the present simple: the train arrives.

rationales.arrives: A future time clause after 'before' normally uses the present simple: the train arrives.
rationales.will arrive: Use the present simple rather than predictive 'will' in this future time clause.
rationales.arriving: 'Arriving' needs a helping verb to complete the clause.

sentence: Please keep your phone quiet ___ the flight.
setupText: Choose the completion that fits the noun phrase 'the flight'.
taskText: Please keep your phone quiet ___ the flight.
text: Choose the completion that fits the noun phrase 'the flight'. Please keep your phone quiet ___ the flight.
explanation: 'During' introduces the noun phrase naming the period of time.

rationales.while: 'While' normally needs a clause here, such as 'while you are on the flight'.
rationales.when: 'When' needs a clause or a different reduced structure; 'the flight' alone does not complete it here.
rationales.during: 'During' introduces the noun phrase naming the period of time.
rationales.as soon as: 'As soon as' needs an event clause, such as 'as soon as the flight begins'.

sentence: Send me a message ___ you land, so I know you've arrived safely.
setupText: Choose the connector that means immediately after the named event.
taskText: Send me a message ___ you land, so I know you've arrived safely.
text: Choose the connector that means immediately after the named event. Send me a message ___ you land, so I know you've arrived safely.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-a2-510:As soon as for prompt action
explanation: As soon as asks for the message immediately after landing.

rationales.long before: Long before would put the message well ahead of landing.
rationales.as soon as: As soon as asks for the message immediately after landing.
rationales.unless: Unless makes landing an exception to sending, rather than the trigger.
rationales.even though: Even though introduces a contrast and does not specify prompt timing.

sentence: I've lived in this building ___ I moved to this city.
setupText: Choose the word giving the starting point of a continuing situation.
taskText: I've lived in this building ___ I moved to this city.
text: Choose the word giving the starting point of a continuing situation. I've lived in this building ___ I moved to this city.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-a2-511:Since introduces the start of a continuing state
explanation: Since introduces the past event from which the residence continues to now.

rationales.until: Until marks an endpoint and would not give the requested beginning of the continuing residence.
rationales.during: During takes a noun phrase, not the full clause I moved to this city.
rationales.before: Before places residence earlier than the move instead of starting with it.
rationales.since: Since introduces the past event from which the residence continues to now.

sentence: The course covers both speaking ___ listening.
setupText: Choose the completion that says the course includes the two skills.
taskText: The course covers both speaking ___ listening.
text: Choose the completion that says the course includes the two skills. The course covers both speaking ___ listening.
explanation: Both ... and includes the two named skills.

rationales.and: Both ... and includes the two named skills.
rationales.or: Or offers alternatives and does not complete the both ... and pair.
rationales.but: But introduces a contrast instead of completing this inclusion structure.
rationales.nor: Nor belongs in a negative pairing such as neither ... nor, not both ... nor.

sentence: You can come either on Tuesday ___ on Thursday.
setupText: Choose the completion that presents two available appointment days.
taskText: You can come either on Tuesday ___ on Thursday.
text: Choose the completion that presents two available appointment days. You can come either on Tuesday ___ on Thursday.
explanation: Either ... or presents Tuesday and Thursday as the available alternatives.

rationales.nor: Nor follows neither in a negative pair, not either in this offer.
rationales.and: And adds both days instead of completing the alternative pair either ... or.
rationales.or: Either ... or presents Tuesday and Thursday as the available alternatives.
rationales.but: But introduces contrast rather than completing the paired choice.

sentence: The apartment has neither a lift ___ a balcony.
setupText: Choose the completion that says both facilities are absent.
taskText: The apartment has neither a lift ___ a balcony.
text: Choose the completion that says both facilities are absent. The apartment has neither a lift ___ a balcony.
explanation: Neither ... nor excludes both the lift and the balcony.

rationales.and: And does not complete the standard neither ... nor pairing.
rationales.nor: Neither ... nor excludes both the lift and the balcony.
rationales.but: But introduces contrast rather than a second item covered by neither.
rationales.also: Also adds information but does not complete the negative pairing neither ... nor.

sentence: The hotel room was small. ___, it had a beautiful view.
setupText: Choose the word that signals a contrast between the two sentences.
taskText: The hotel room was small. ___, it had a beautiful view.
text: Choose the word that signals a contrast between the two sentences. The hotel room was small. ___, it had a beautiful view.
explanation: However introduces a positive feature that balances the small room.

rationales.Therefore: Therefore makes the view a result of the room being small.
rationales.For example: For example would make the view an example of small size.
rationales.Then: Then orders events in time rather than contrasting two features.
rationales.However: However introduces a positive feature that balances the small room.

sentence: The shop repairs phones. It ___ sells chargers.
setupText: Choose the word that adds another service.
taskText: The shop repairs phones. It ___ sells chargers.
text: Choose the word that adds another service. The shop repairs phones. It ___ sells chargers.
explanation: Also adds charger sales to phone repairs.

rationales.also: Also adds charger sales to phone repairs.
rationales.instead: Instead would replace repairing phones with selling chargers.
rationales.otherwise: Otherwise introduces an alternative situation or consequence, not another service.
rationales.therefore: Therefore presents sales as a conclusion from repairs, rather than simply adding information.

sentence: We didn't go to the cinema. We watched a film at home ___.
setupText: Choose the word showing that a new plan replaced the old one.
taskText: We didn't go to the cinema. We watched a film at home ___.
text: Choose the word showing that a new plan replaced the old one. We didn't go to the cinema. We watched a film at home ___.
explanation: Instead identifies watching at home as the substitute for going to the cinema.

rationales.too: Too would add home viewing to a cinema visit, but the visit did not happen.
rationales.therefore: Therefore presents a conclusion and is not the natural sentence-final replacement marker here.
rationales.instead: Instead identifies watching at home as the substitute for going to the cinema.
rationales.for example: For example would introduce an instance of a broader category, not the replacement plan.

sentence: You can borrow tools here, ___ a hammer or a drill.
setupText: Choose the phrase introducing specific examples of tools.
taskText: You can borrow tools here, ___ a hammer or a drill.
text: Choose the phrase introducing specific examples of tools. You can borrow tools here, ___ a hammer or a drill.
explanation: Such as introduces a hammer and a drill as examples of tools.

rationales.because of: Because of would make the tools a reason for borrowing rather than examples.
rationales.such as: Such as introduces a hammer and a drill as examples of tools.
rationales.instead of: Instead of would present these tools as things replaced, not things included.
rationales.as soon as: As soon as introduces a time clause, not a list of examples.

sentence: I left my wallet on the train. ___, a passenger handed it to the station staff.
setupText: Choose the phrase that moves the story forward in time.
taskText: I left my wallet on the train. ___, a passenger handed it to the station staff.
text: Choose the phrase that moves the story forward in time. I left my wallet on the train. ___, a passenger handed it to the station staff.
explanation: An hour later places the handover after the wallet was left behind.

rationales.For that reason: For that reason states a causal link rather than giving the requested later time.
rationales.In contrast: In contrast compares differences rather than advancing this sequence.
rationales.For example: For example would introduce an illustration, not the next event.
rationales.An hour later: An hour later places the handover after the wallet was left behind.

sentence: I wanted enough space for my work equipment.
setupText: Choose the sentence that describes the purpose of buying a larger bag.
taskText: I wanted enough space for my work equipment.
text: Choose the sentence that describes the purpose of buying a larger bag. I wanted enough space for my work equipment.
options: I bought a larger bag although I could carry my equipment.
I bought a larger bag so that I could carry my equipment.
I bought a larger bag after I carried my equipment.
I bought a larger bag, but I couldn't carry my equipment.
answer: I bought a larger bag so that I could carry my equipment.
explanation: So that I could states the intended use that motivated the purchase.

rationales.I bought a larger bag so that I could ca: So that I could states the intended use that motivated the purchase.
rationales.I bought a larger bag although I could c: Although presents carrying as an existing ability in contrast, not the purchase's purpose.
rationales.I bought a larger bag after I carried my: After gives a sequence without stating the intended use.
rationales.I bought a larger bag, but I couldn't ca: But reports an unsuccessful result rather than explaining the goal.
